sections.hypothesis: Trend-vol-target on BTC, ETH and SOL earns more in its textbook symmetric form, long when its trends are up and short when they are down, than long-only. Hypothetical: Kestrel can't short (P5 parked; retail shorting in Australia is CFDs at 2:1, real perps are wholesale-only). A pass is recorded as needs-shorting and never traded until a licensed retail route exists and Luke has checked the Swyftx employee trading policy.
sections.rationale: Who pays: as for the long side (under-reaction, late sellers, forced deleveraging). Outside evidence: the symmetric sign rule is the one Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen (2012) tested, and both legs earned. Not a rejected family. Disclosed: this changes the long side too (with 2 of 3 trends up it holds 1/3, not 2/3), so the comparison is the whole rule against the pursued one, not a short leg bolted on. Runs: one, three trials (BTC, ETH, SOL) in the main log.
sections.rules: Votes as trend-vol-target: for each lookback (20, 60, 120 days), +1 if the close is above the close that many days earlier, -1 if below. Weight = (sum of votes) / 3 x min(1, 50% / annualised volatility of the last 30 daily log returns): from -1 to +1. Cash until the lookbacks and the volatility window have filled. BTC, ETH and SOL, each separately. Decide at each close, trade at the next open (the engine's convention); returns open to open, daily, 2020-01-01 to 2025-10-31 (Binance funding history starts 2020-01; nothing from the holdout). Weights in [-1, 1]: short notional never above equity, inside ASIC's 2:1 retail cap (margin 50% of notional). A short is closed out if a day's high reaches 1.5x its entry (a conservative 2:1 margin call), at that price.
sections.parameters: fast_days 20, mid_days 60, slow_days 120, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50 (the pursued settings). Nothing else is tried.
sections.costs: Long side as kestrel.toml (7.5 bps fee with the BNB discount plus the coin's half-spread band, on every change in weight). Short side, primary (the retail route: a 2:1 CFD like Eightcap's): 2x the coin's spot half-spread band on every change in short weight (CFD spreads are wider than spot; no commission) plus financing of 5% a year on short notional, charged daily (Eightcap's trade page lists a 5% p.a. BTC swap; whether that is the short rate is unconfirmed: check before freezing). Reported, deciding nothing (same signals, so not extra trials): the short as a Binance USDT-M perp (5 bps taker per side plus the band, and its real 8-hourly funding: a positive rate pays the short), and the CFD at 15% a year (an older Eightcap rate).
